title: Negative: the wave-pinning crawler does not re-nucleate its front. A front cut splits the polarity, and the cell rounds up into a static, uniformly polarized disk or divides into two such disks. Erasing the polarity kills the cell within one time unit. Only a rear cut keeps it crawling.
summary: Camley et al. crawler (world.py: chi=0.25, L=5, N=256, with a per-body well-mixed pool). Each cut is applied at t=8 to a mature half-moon (speed 0.30), against a branched undamaged twin, on seeds 0 and 1. Erased protein leaves the cell (C' = C - lost). (a) A 30% front sector (20-21% of the area, 22-24% of the protein) leaves the polarity domain as two lateral lobes that pull the cell into a dumbbell. One lobe wins, the cell rounds up, rho floods to the uniform high state and the cell stops: speed 0.00-0.03 against the twin's 0.30 at t=16, with polarized area = whole cell (v2_s*_front30/cut.png). (b) A 15% front sector (9% of the area) splits the cell into two round, static, uniform-high daughters on both seeds (v2_s*_front15). (c) Erasing the whole bound polarity domain chemically ('chem', shape kept, 22% of the protein): the low state is linearly stable, so the whole boundary retracts at rho* and the cell vanishes by t=8.95 on both seeds, with no re-nucleation (v2_s*_chem). (d) Weak noise eta on rho, single seed (global-pool code, identical for one body): at eta=4 and 6 the chem-cut cell still dies within 1.1, and at eta=6 the twin slows to 0.13. At eta=8 and 10 noise keeps the cut cell alive as a noisy static disk, but the twin also stops (0.02). So no noise level re-nucleates a crawling front while the twin still crawls. At eta=4 the front-cut cell stays a static disk for 12 time units. (e) A 30% rear sector (15-16% of the area) never touches the polarity: the cell keeps crawling at 0.27-0.28, reshaped smaller (area 2.14 vs 2.52). That is shape smoothing by curvature flow, by construction. (f) The linear-kinetics twin (KIN=1) depolarizes by t~0.5 and sits as a static round cell (displacement 0.002 in t=10). Mechanism: wave pinning gives two coexisting attractors, a polarized crawler and a uniform-high disk; damage to the front moves the cell to the second, and the protein lost with the cut narrows the cell's allowed-area window (C'/3, C'/2), so the polarized state is not regained. Limits: deterministic dynamics, so seeds 0 and 1 differ only in heading and initial noise; cut at a single time; no labkit packs; chi=0.25 rather than the paper's 0.3 (see the parent sighting).

finding.operator: mass-conserved bistable (wave-pinning) polarity driving an Allen-Cahn cell boundary
finding.control: branched undamaged twins on 2 seeds; linear-kinetics twin; noise sweep eta 0-10
finding.result: front cut 20%/9% area: static uniform-high disk (speed <=0.03 vs twin 0.30) or fission into two static disks, 2/2 seeds each; chem erase: extinct by dt=0.95, 2/2; rear cut 15%: crawls at 0.27-0.28 (twin 0.30), 2/2; no eta keeps the twin crawling and re-nucleates the cut cell
